column1: # Consolidate the isolated string-fragment FIRST_ROW leaf under the Datum-backed aggregate runtime.

column9: The Datum-backed state replaces the string-fragment leaf and adds direct fold plus source-compatible Int, Float64, and String spill seams; parser reachability, eager expression resolution, and unrepresented Go typed domains remain partial.
Merge and first-row semantics now execute over typed Datum values rather than string fragments.
The first retained String payload charge is asserted while Go per-type allocation layouts and executor memory tracking remain partial.
Decimal remains partial because Rust does not reproduce Go MyDecimal's raw in-memory spill encoding.
The exact Int spill fixtures now round-trip through Go's field order and native encoding.
Time remains partial until Datum owns a typed temporal representation.
The exact source long string, Go field order, native length, raw bytes, and reusable buffer growth now execute.
Float32 stays partial instead of being erased into the f64 Datum variant.
Raw Float64 payloads now round-trip through Go's field order and native encoding.
Duration stays partial until Datum owns duration and FSP together.
JSON stays partial until Datum owns BinaryJSON type-code and payload.
Enum stays partial until Datum owns name and numeric identity.
Set stays partial until Datum owns name and numeric identity.
